title: Cluster networking: pod-to-pod traffic, CNI and choosing a plugin

videos.script: Kubernetes makes one promise about the network, and leaves the rest to a plugin. {{promise}} The promise: every pod gets its own address, and every pod can reach every other pod at that address, on any node, with no translation in between. {{no-nat}} How that is kept depends on the plugin. The one on the laptop's cluster does the simplest thing there is: it gives each node a range of addresses, and writes a route on every node to every other node's range. {{routes}} You will send a packet from a pod on one node to a pod on another, and read each hop it takes. {{hops}} Then you will compare the plugins clusters actually choose between, and what makes each one worth its cost. {{compare}}
